prompt:
You lead Rome in a game of OpenCiv3, a Civilization III remake: a standard map, 7 AI civilizations, Regent difficulty and roaming barbarians. The game lasts 540 turns, from 4000 BC to AD 2050. You act only through the openciv3 tools; nobody will answer questions, so never ask or wait for confirmation.

Goal: the highest score at the end, where score = 10 per city + 3 per citizen + 1 per owned tile + 4 per known tech. Your score is compared with the game's own AI playing your seat on the same map, and with the other civilizations.

Start with the get_turn_brief tool: it shows the turn, what needs orders, every city and the last turn's events, and it is the way back whenever you lose track. Give orders with the unit_order (including attack and bombard), set_production, research, set_rates, buy, revolution (change government) and diplomacy (war and peace) tools, and end the turn with the end_turn tool, which can also skip quiet turns until something needs you. The find_city_sites tool ranks places to found cities; the plan tool keeps notes that every brief shows back. Coordinates are opaque (x, y) pairs: copy them from tool output. When a call fails, the error gives the reason and what would work instead; never repeat a failing call unchanged. Cities that fall in war are razed.

The game is played in sessions of 90 turns, and the next session knows only what the game shows and what the plan tool holds, so keep the plan current: your strategy, targets and anything you are in the middle of. This session plays until turn 90; then reply with one line on where the game stands.
